frontier_selector.champion: Inflammatory Carcinoma of the Breast with Cutaneous Metastasis
frontier_selector.why: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, as seen in the skin biopsy, is a decisive finding that points towards a diagnosis of Inflammatory Carcinoma of the Breast with Cutaneous Metastasis.

support_spans: pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
A well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque, 15 × 12 cm, was seen over the right side of the anterior chest wall around her operation scar
Scattered within the erythema were multiple palpable small nodules
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
contradict_spans: Negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)
